result:
Solution 3 gives the answer I believe is correct. I checked its argument and also recall the literature result that a general such surface has exactly two genus 2 pencils. I did not re-derive that literature result, so the recollection is the less certain part.

**Why Solution 3 holds up.** A genus 2 fiber class F satisfies F² = 0 and K·F = 2. Given one pencil F₀, the class δ = F₀ − 2K has δ² = −4 and K·δ = 0. For a general surface, the Néron–Severi group is ℤK ⊕ ℤδ. Writing F = aK + bδ, the conditions force a = 2 and b = ±1. So there are exactly two candidate classes, F₀ and F₁ = 4K − F₀.

To show F₁ is also a pencil, the solution restricts to the canonical curve C. Because q = 0, K_S|_C is an even theta characteristic, so h⁰(K_S|_C) = 0. A Riemann–Roch and vanishing computation then gives h⁰(F₁) = 2. Since F₁² = 0 and there are no (−2)-curves, |F₁| is a base-point-free pencil, which makes F₁ a second genus 2 fibration.

**Why Solution 2 fails.** It finds the same two candidates but computes h⁰(4K − F₁) = 1. This is wrong because it uses 4K − F₁ with F₁ the first pencil, and it applies a generic h¹ = 0 claim without justification. Solution 3's explicit computation with the theta characteristic shows the h⁰ is 2.

**Why Solution 1 fails.** It cites results that do not say what it claims, and its "exactly 4" is unsupported.

CHOICE: 3
